learning_outcomes.text: Students will gain knowledge about the economic analysis of a system and a process.
Students will acquire the skill to identify, define, and solve chemical engineering economics problems.
Students will learn capital cost estimation.
Students will gain knowledge about depreciation calculations.
Students will be able to perform profitability analysis.

syllabus_topics: Cost and Asset Accounting: Accounting procedure, Basic Relationships, Balance Sheet, Income Statements, Cost Accounting Methods
Cost Estimation 1: Factors Affecting Cash Flow, Investment and Production Costs
Cost Estimation 2: Capital Investment, Estimation of Capital Investment, Cost Indicators
Cost Estimation 3: Cost Components in Capital Investment
Cost Estimation 4: Capital Investment Estimation Methods
Cost Estimation 5: Estimation of Total Product Cost

Interest, Time Value of Money: Types of Interest, Simple Interest, Compound Interest, Nominal and Effective Interest Rates, Continuous Interest, Present Value and Discounting, Equal Period-End Payments
Depreciation: Types of Depreciation, Service Life, Salvage Value, Present Value, Depreciation Calculation Methods
bibliography: Peters, M.S., Timmerhaus, K.D., Plant Design and Economics for Chemical Engineers, McGraw-Hill Book Company, Inc., Singapore, 2003.
Kurtz, M.P.E., Calculations for Engineering Economic Analysis, McGraw-Hill, Inc., N.Y., 1995.
Garrett, D., Chemical Engineering Economics, Van Nostrand Reinhold, N. Y.,1989.
